vignette:
Arjun sits quietly in the therapy room, his gaze fixed on the floor. He is twenty-two, a student studying international relations, but his eyes carry the weight of someone much older. The faint hum of the air conditioning interrupts the silence, a stark contrast to the chaos he has witnessed. He shifts in his chair, leaning slightly forward, and begins to recount his time as a relief worker in a war zone—a narrative that has become both a burden and an anchor to his identity.

It all started two years ago when he was fresh out of college, full of idealism and a desire to help those in need. Arjun joined a non-governmental organization that provided humanitarian aid in a conflict-ridden region of his home country. The streets were filled with devastation—a haunting reminder of the violence that had torn through the community. He remembers feeling both exhilarated and terrified when he first arrived, the cacophony of distant gunfire and the sight of crumbling buildings contrasting sharply with the faces of the people he aimed to help.

As weeks turned into months, Arjun found himself immersed in the daily grind of delivering supplies, administering first aid, and offering comfort to those who had lost everything. He recalls one night vividly, a moment that would forever alter the course of his life. The team had set up a makeshift clinic in an abandoned school when the sounds of an explosion echoed nearby. Chaos erupted. In the midst of the panic, he rushed to help a young woman who had been injured. The blood, the screams, the acrid smell of smoke—it all swirled together into a whirlwind of horror that he cannot escape.

After that night, everything changed. Arjun returned home, but he felt like a ghost in his own life. The vibrant campus he once loved now seemed muted, the laughter of his peers an unbearable reminder of what he had witnessed. He struggles to concentrate in class, often staring blankly at the lecture notes, his mind drifting back to the faces of those he could not save. The flashbacks hit him at unexpected moments—while walking to class, during study sessions, even in the safety of his own bedroom. Each memory feels like a jagged shard of glass, cutting through his attempts to find solace.

Sleep eludes him. He tosses and turns, haunted by nightmares that replay the horrors of that night in the clinic. He wakes drenched in sweat, heart racing, as images of the young woman’s bloodied face invade his thoughts. Exhausted, he drags himself through his days, relying on caffeine to keep him awake but feeling increasingly detached from reality. Friends invite him to parties and social gatherings, but he often declines, preferring the solitude of his room. The isolation is a double-edged sword; it shields him from the outside world but deepens the sense of loneliness that gnaws at him.

In therapy, Arjun describes how he feels trapped in a cycle of guilt and shame. He often questions whether he did enough to help, replaying every decision he made that night. The weight of responsibility sits heavily on his shoulders, and he struggles to reconcile his desire to be a force for good with the trauma that now defines him. He shares his shame over his inability to be the strong, resilient worker he once was, feeling as though he has let down not only himself but the very people he set out to help.

His therapist notes the way his eyes light up when he talks about his passion for humanitarian work, even as he wrestles with the shadows of his experiences. Arjun expresses a longing to return to the field, to make a difference, yet he is paralyzed by the fear of encountering similar situations. The internal battle rages on; the desire to help is at odds with his overwhelming anxiety.

As they continue to explore his feelings, Arjun reflects on the importance of finding a way to honor the experiences of those he lost while learning to navigate his own pain. The journey is daunting, but amid the darkness, there is a flicker of hope—a yearning to transform his trauma into a source of strength, to once again step into the world with purpose and compassion.
